data.narrative:
Eridu is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Drew Perkins and Omar Hassen that has raised approximately $230M to date. The broader Chips & Semiconductors sector comprises 11 same-sector peers, including 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The semiconductor universe contains only one same-stage peer and one adjacent-stage peer in Eridu's tier, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold required for reliable median-based triangulation. Expanding the filter to all 11 same-sector peers would introduce material stage and scale heterogeneity that would obscure rather than inform valuation. The public comparables span vastly different market capitalizations and business models, limiting their direct relevance to a Series A private company.

Without sufficient narrow-peer density or applicable quantitative methods from the available data, a triangulated valuation range cannot be defensibly derived. Key uncertainties include whether the large public peers (NVDA, AMD) command valuations reflective of Eridu's technology differentiation and market position, and whether the identified private peers—operating at different stages and with different capital efficiency—represent meaningful anchors. Additional disclosure regarding Eridu's revenue, burn rate, or specific technical achievements would be necessary to support a rigorous valuation range.
